summary: Expanded AGENT_ROLES in constants.ts from 7 to 9 entries (added Security Auditor, Release Engineer in canonical order).

Added optional active_pipeline_stages parameter to ledger_create_work_package (work-package.ts) with hard guardrails (empty, duplicates, invalid types, out-of-order) and soft warnings (implementation without qa, single-stage chain).
Updated startPipeline to read WP active_pipeline_stages, validate requested type against active stages, and use resolvePrerequisite() for dynamic ordering check.

Updated completePipeline to generalize auto-finalize (any terminal stage agent, not just Documentation), route handoff notes via resolveFailAgent/resolveNextAgent, emit soft warning for empty artifacts.files_modified, and pass activeStages to buildCompletionGuidance.

Rewrote buildCompletionGuidance to use dynamic terminal stage detection via CANONICAL_PIPELINE_ORDERING filter (.at(-1)) and resolve next/fail agents dynamically — activeStages added as last param with default for backward compat.
Updated hasDownstreamFail, checkRevalidationGuard, and hasDownstreamReengagedSince in workflow-helpers.ts to accept optional activeStages param, removing legacy FAIL_ROUTING_MAP usage.

Updated getDeveloperAction and getQaAction in workflow-next-action.ts to skip WPs where their pipeline type is not active, derive qaPrerequisite via resolvePrerequisite(), and pass activeStages to downstream fail checks.
Updated getReviewerAction to add active stages filter, dynamic reviewPrerequisite, and upstream rework limit checks based on active upstream stages.
Added getSecurityAuditorAction (mirrors QA, no self-rework on fail) and getReleaseEngineerAction (self-rework on fail, mirrors Documentation structure).

Updated getDocumentationAction to add active stages filter, dynamic docPrerequisite, generalized freshness check (firstActiveStage instead of hardcoded implementation), and upstream rework limit checks.
Added Security Auditor and Release Engineer cases to getNextAction switch statement.
Updated help-content.ts ledger_create_work_package entry with active_pipeline_stages parameter docs and examples.
All 1241 tests pass; clean TypeScript build with no errors.

summary: Reviewed all 6 modified files across 4 focus areas identified by QA. Core routing logic is correct and backward-compatible. All 10 acceptance criteria were verified independently.

FOCUS 1 — resolveFailAgent fallback (pipeline-maps.ts:218–229): Logic is correct. Base agent ↔ stage reverse-lookup via AGENT_PIPELINE_MAP is sound for all 6 types. Fallback to first-active-stage owner when standard fail-target stage absent is well-designed. One semantic edge case noted below (non-blocking).

FOCUS 2 — buildCompletionGuidance terminal-stage detection (pipeline.ts:471–495): Correct. orderedActive.at(-1) pattern cleanly identifies the terminal stage dynamically. A QA-only WP (activeStages=['qa']) correctly produces isTerminalStage=true for type='qa'. PM overrides bypass auto-finalize intentionally — confirmed by isTerminalAgent check.

FOCUS 3 — getSecurityAuditorAction: Correctly mirrors getQaAction. P5 (WAIT_FOR_REWORK) confirms no self-rework on fail — 'Developer must address findings before Security Auditor can retry.' P4 re-engagement (hasNewUpstreamPassSince) is structurally identical to getQaAction. Verified.

FOCUS 4 — getDocumentationAction firstActiveStage freshness check: Correctly replaces hardcoded 'implementation'. For documentation-only WPs (firstActiveStage='documentation'), the freshness check compares doc PASS completion vs doc pipeline start — always true, which is correct. Stale/rework detection still works correctly for multi-stage WPs.

comments.note: workflow-helpers.ts checkRevalidationGuard Step 5: `getUpstreamTypes(pipelineType)` is called WITHOUT forwarding the `activeStages` parameter, yet `hasDownstreamFail` in Step 4 correctly forwards it. For non-default stage WPs that include 'security-audit' or 'release-engineering' in upstream positions, those stage types will be absent from the `upstreamTypes` array (which uses DEFAULT_PIPELINE_STAGES), causing the upstream-rework check to silently miss them. Impact is conservative (false negative — allows a pipeline that may need revalidation), but it is a partial implementation gap for the feature this WP introduces. Fix: change `getUpstreamTypes(pipelineType)` to `getUpstreamTypes(pipelineType, activeStages ?? DEFAULT_PIPELINE_STAGES)`. Recommend tracking as tech-debt in WP-006.

GetNextActionSchema agent_role .describe() text (workflow-next-action.ts ~line 42) still lists only 7 roles: 'Planner, Project Manager, Developer, QA, Reviewer, Documentation, Synthesis' — omitting 'Security Auditor' and 'Release Engineer'. This string is surfaced via MCP to calling agents; Security Auditor and Release Engineer personas may not know these roles are valid. The runtime error message at line 67 does enumerate all AGENT_ROLES correctly, so there is a recovery path, but the description should be updated. Non-blocking since actual Zod validation accepts all 9 roles.

StartPipelineSchema and CompletePipelineSchema type parameter .describe() text still enumerates only 4 pipeline types: 'implementation, qa, code-review, documentation' — omitting 'security-audit' and 'release-engineering'. The PipelineTypeEnum Zod validation is correct and accepts all 6 types, but the guidance text surfaced to MCP tool callers is stale. Update these two .describe() strings to list all 6 types.

constants.ts JSDoc comment at line 5 still reads 'the seven-stage workflow agent roles' after AGENT_ROLES was expanded from 7 to 9 entries. Should be updated to '9-role' or 'multi-role' to avoid confusion with the previous 7-role count.

resolveFailAgent fallback edge case: for WPs where QA or Security Auditor is the first active stage and implementation is absent (e.g. activeStages=['qa','code-review']), resolveFailAgent('qa', activeStages) routes back to 'QA' (first active stage owner). buildCompletionGuidance then emits self-rework guidance for QA, contradicting the 'QA does not self-rework' design documented in getQaAction P5. This edge case requires an unusual WP composition (non-implementation-first) and is conservative behavior (QA still processes the FAIL), but the guidance text is semantically misleading. Non-blocking.

CANONICAL_PIPELINE_ORDERING.filter() pattern for computing orderedActive / upstreamActiveStages is duplicated across getReviewerAction, getReleaseEngineerAction, and getDocumentationAction in workflow-next-action.ts. All three compute the same orderedActive slice before their respective index lookups. Developer and QA both noted this. A shared helper (e.g. getUpstreamStages(type, activeStages)) would reduce 9+ lines of identical logic to a single call per function. Good candidate for WP-006 or a follow-on micro-WP.
